document.title: Talking Points
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), New Documents Detail America's Strategic Response to 9/11
document.note: [Secret] Talking points for Secretary Powell drafted two days after 9/11. Objectives include eliminating bin Laden's al-Qaida. Focus is on regional support from Pakistan, India and Bangladesh and cooperation with Saudi Arabia and Egypt; the U.S. will also probe Iran's ability to work against the Taliban and bin Laden.

events.description: Terrorist attacks on the United States, referred to as the attacks of September 11, which prompted the US response campaign.
State Department talking points prepared for the Secretary's press conference on the US response and coalition-building.
US took a tough line with Pakistan during the week after 9/11, and Armitage was to ask Mahmud for specific comments.
Armitage spoke to Russian DFM Trubnikov to prepare for his trip to Moscow.
Planned meeting with Chinese Foreign Minister Tang Jiaxuan to press for public support.
Planned G-8 Foreign Ministers meeting in New York to produce a strong condemnation of global terrorism.
Attacks on the United States referenced as basis for the campaign.
State Department talking points set objectives to eliminate al-Qaida and terrorist safehavens.
President contacted Putin, Blair, Schroeder, Chretien, Chirac; Secretary spoke with Kofi Annan and EU leaders.
US took a tough line with Pakistan during the week.
Armitage to ask Mahmud for specific comments 'today'; possible call to Musharraf.
Armitage spoke to Trubnikov ahead of trip to Moscow.
Planned meeting with Chinese FM Tang Jiaxuan.
G-8 Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York to produce condemnation of terrorism.
Planned visit of Indonesian President Megawati the following week.
Planned meeting with Sudanese FM Ismail in New York.

Public Diplomacy campaign document (attached, not included)
key_claims: US policy objectives after 9/11 included holding accountable those who harbor the attackers and eliminating bin-Laden's al-Qaida.
The State Department took a tough line with Pakistan, with Armitage seeking specific comments from Mahmud and a possible call to Musharraf.
Russia and the Central Asian states were identified as partners to increase pressure on the Taliban and bin-Laden.
The US planned to probe whether Iran could work with it against the Taliban and bin-Laden.
The US aimed to strengthen UNSCR 1333 and build UN support for retaliation against bin-Laden's organization and the Taliban regime.
